content.user_title: Retrieve Lark Meeting Notes and Transcripts
content.value_statement: Meeting records are difficult to retrieve when note types and document tokens vary. This skill uses an explicit note_id to find details and route transcript access correctly.
actual_capabilities: Queries Lark Note details using an explicit note_id.
Returns the note display type and available document tokens.
Routes normal transcripts to their separate document token.
Retrieves unified transcripts through the Lark Note transcript command.
Explains routes from meeting, minute, event, or document identifiers.
limitations: Requires lark-cli, user authentication, and permission to access the requested note.
Cannot discover notes from a natural-language title alone.
Does not infer note_id from document tokens, titles, text, or backlinks.
Delegates document body reading and upstream identifier discovery to other Lark skills.

use_cases.title: Inspect meeting note assets
use_cases.description: Retrieve note type and document tokens before opening summaries, transcripts, or shared files.

use_cases.title: Review exact discussion
use_cases.description: Select the correct transcript route and retrieve speaker-level meeting records.

use_cases.title: Build reliable note workflows
use_cases.description: Resolve explicit identifiers and avoid incorrect routing between normal and unified notes.

prompt_templates.title: Look up note details
prompt_templates.prompt: Use note_id {note_id} to retrieve the display type and all available document tokens. Summarize the result.
prompt_templates.scenario: Basic lookup with a known note identifier

prompt_templates.title: Choose a transcript route
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect note_id {note_id}. Retrieve its transcript through the correct route for normal, unknown, or unified display types.

prompt_templates.title: Follow a document reference
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the explicit vc-node-id {vc_node_id} from fetched document markup. Retrieve the matching note details and explain the next route.
prompt_templates.scenario: Lookup from a verified document reference

prompt_templates.title: Audit transcript retrieval
prompt_templates.prompt: For note_id {note_id}, explain the selected transcript route. Retrieve complete content and report the output location or failure without partial results.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced retrieval with route and failure reporting

output_examples.output: Display type: unified. Main note document: docus_main. Retrieve the transcript through the unified transcript route.

output_examples.input: Get the transcript for a normal note with verbatim document docus_verbatim.
output_examples.output: The transcript is a separate document. Read docus_verbatim through the document workflow.

best_practices: Provide an exact note_id or an explicit vc-node-id from fetched document markup.
Retrieve note details before choosing a transcript route.
Use the authenticated user identity and verify access to sensitive meeting content.
anti_patterns: Do not infer note_id from a title, document token, text, or backlink.
Do not pass a minute token as a note identifier.
Do not identify unified notes from verbatim_doc_token presence alone.

faq.question: What identifier does this skill require?
faq.answer: It requires an explicit note_id or a verified vc-node-id from fetched document markup.

faq.question: Can it find a note by title?
faq.answer: No. Use a Lark document search workflow first, then return with an explicit vc-node-id.

faq.question: How does it choose the transcript route?
faq.answer: It checks note_display_type. Normal notes use a document token, while unified notes use the Note transcript workflow.

faq.question: Where are unified transcripts saved?
faq.answer: They are saved under the local notes directory as Markdown, or as text when plain text format is selected.

faq.question: Does it overwrite existing transcript files?
faq.answer: No. Existing files cause an error unless the user explicitly requests overwrite behavior.

faq.question: What access does it need?
faq.answer: It needs lark-cli, an authenticated user identity, and permission to read the requested Lark meeting content.
